issues.legal_issue: A prescribed authority must give effect to a release order that has become final after challenges to it have failed.
material_facts: The appellate authority ordered the release of part of a tenanted building and directed that the building be divided accordingly.
Challenges to that order, including a special leave petition, failed before the authority began proceedings to implement the division.
The prescribed authority rejected the tenant’s request not to proceed with the division.
issues.conclusion: The prescribed authority was bound to implement the final release order and did not act outside its jurisdiction or contrary to law by doing so.
issues.legal_principle: A final order that has survived the available challenges binds the authority responsible for implementing it. Section 24 of the U.P. Urban Building Act, 1972 was invoked to argue that the prescribed authority retained control over the ejectment proceedings, but the Court rejected that contention. No earlier cases were cited.

predicates.post_finality_implementation_proceeding: A proceeding was brought before an authority to implement a release order after the challenges to that order had concluded.
predicates.release_order_became_final: An order releasing premises became final after challenges to it failed.
predicates.authority_was_implementing_order: The authority was carrying out the directions in the final release order.

issues.definition: When an authority is implementing a release order in a post-finality proceeding and that order has become final, the authority must implement it.

issues.legal_issue: A subsequent event cannot reopen a release order that became final before the event occurred.
material_facts: A landlord’s personal-need release proceeding resulted in a final order releasing part of the accommodation.
The order became final after the tenant’s challenges failed.
The landlord died after the release order had become final, while steps to divide the premises were underway.
The tenant asked the prescribed authority to stop the division because of the landlord’s death.
issues.conclusion: Although subsequent events must be considered in proceedings still being considered, the landlord’s death did not permit the already-final release proceeding to be reopened.
issues.legal_principle: Subsequent events must be taken into account by a statutory authority or court when considering a landlord’s petition to eject a tenant on the ground of the landlord’s personal need. That principle does not authorize reopening a controversy concluded by an order that became final before the subsequent event. No earlier cases were cited.

predicates.landlord_personal_need_proceeding: A proceeding concerned a landlord’s request to recover premises for personal need.
predicates.subsequent_event_arose: An event relevant to the claim occurred after the release order was made.
predicates.final_order_preceded_event: The release order became final before the subsequent event occurred.

issues.definition: If a relevant event occurs after a final order in a landlord’s personal-need proceeding, the final release proceeding cannot be reopened because of that event.

issues.legal_issue: An appeal confined to a later implementation decision does not permit reopening an earlier release proceeding that has become final.
material_facts: The tenant’s appeal arose from the rejection of an application made after the release proceedings had become final.
The application sought to prevent implementation of the final order because of the landlord’s subsequent death.
The appeal was confined to the question arising from that later application.
issues.conclusion: The Court could not reopen the release proceeding that had become final; it had to decide only the question arising from the later application.
issues.legal_principle: A court deciding an appeal limited to an issue arising after the underlying release proceeding became final must confine itself to that issue and cannot reopen the concluded proceeding. No earlier cases were cited.

predicates.appeal_from_post_finality_application: An appeal arose from a decision on an application made after the release proceeding had become final.
predicates.appeal_limited_to_later_issue: The appeal concerned only the issue arising from that later application.
predicates.underlying_release_proceeding_final: The proceeding that produced the release order had become final before the later application was made.

issues.definition: When an appeal concerns only an issue raised by a post-finality application, the court cannot reopen the underlying release proceeding if it had already become final.
